images.name: duties
images.title: A recruiting agency, *duty by duty*
rows: Turns the client's request into a job order. Missing details go to the recruiter.
Asks every applicant the client's written requirements and logs each answer.
Books, confirms, reminds and reschedules both sides.
Requests references, collects forms and keeps each file's checklist.
Texts available, qualified workers and books the first to confirm.
Prepares the file. A recruiter decides and makes the call.

head: Desk
The AI Employee handles
It hands to a recruiter
rows: Fills shifts, confirms start times, chases timesheets
Collects paperwork, tracks end dates, asks about extensions
images.source: Examples. Every agency sets its own rules.

images.name: monday
images.title: A Monday at a *staffing agency*
rows: A forklift operator is a no-show. It texts four available workers and books one by 6:20.
Asks 42 overnight applicants the client's knockout questions for a receptionist role.
A candidate has a competing offer. It sends the client's feedback to the recruiter.
Books six interviews and sends reminders for tomorrow's panel.
A background check comes back flagged. It goes to the recruiter untouched.
Tells three candidates from last week where they stand.
A client is unhappy with a temp. It books a call with the account owner.

images.name: setup
images.title: How it *is set up* at an agency
steps: Tag ATS activity: screening, scheduling, references, shifts, timesheets.
Only job-related requirements, the same for every applicant.
ATS, email, texting and calendars. No submitting, no offers.
Submissions, judgment calls, pay and complaints go to a named recruiter.
It drafts every message and rejection while a recruiter reads each one.
Check a sample against the rules and update them as clients change.
